summary: Ground DefectDojo upstream specs for endpoint/metrics/generic-parser/extra-parsers before strict-TDD ports

key_behaviors: URL parsing via hyperlink.parse() with fallback to urllib.parse for UnicodeDecodeError
from_uri() method parses URI strings into 7 components: protocol, userinfo, host, port, path, query, fragment
Default port inference via SCHEME_PORT_MAP (http=80, https=443) - stored explicitly if provided, omitted if matches scheme default
clean() method normalizes path by stripping leading slashes, validates all components against RFC3986 regexes, enforces non-null host, converts port to int
__str__() method reconstructs URL using hyperlink.EncodedURL with normalize() call, handles null protocol case by stripping dummy scheme
__hash__() delegates to __str__().__hash__()
__eq__() compares string representation and product_id (if both present), returns NotImplemented for non-Endpoint types
endpoint_filter() function handles optional fields by filtering null vs exact match, applies SCHEME_PORT_MAP logic for port matching across products
Endpoint_Status fields track vulnerability status (mitigated, false_positive, risk_accepted, out_of_scope) with audit trail (mitigated_by, mitigated_time, last_modified, date)
fields: Endpoint.protocol (CharField, null/blank) - scheme like http, https, ftp, dns per RFC3986 pattern [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9.+-]*
Endpoint.userinfo (CharField max 500, null/blank) - user:password pair per RFC3986 pattern [A-Za-z0-9.-_~%!$&'()*+,;=:]+
Endpoint.host (CharField max 500, null/blank=False required) - FQDN or IPv4/IPv6 per RFC3986 pattern [A-Za-z0-9_+-][A-Za-z0-9_.-+]+
Endpoint.port (IntegerField, null/blank) - integer 0-65535, stored as explicit int or null
Endpoint.path (CharField max 500, null/blank) - root-less path without leading slash per RFC3986 pattern
Endpoint.query (CharField max 1000, null/blank) - key=value pairs joined by & without leading ?
Endpoint.fragment (CharField max 500, null/blank) - anchor identifier without leading #
Endpoint_Status.date (DateField, default=get_current_date) - date endpoint status created
Endpoint_Status.last_modified (DateTimeField, editable=False, default=get_current_datetime) - auto-updated on save
Endpoint_Status.mitigated_time (DateTimeField, editable=False, null/blank) - timestamp when marked mitigated
Endpoint_Status.mitigated_by (ForeignKey Dojo_User, null, RESTRICT) - user who mitigated
Endpoint_Status.false_positive (BooleanField, default=False) - finding is false positive
Endpoint_Status.out_of_scope (BooleanField, default=False) - finding is out of scope
Endpoint_Status.risk_accepted (BooleanField, default=False) - finding is risk accepted
Endpoint_Status.endpoint (ForeignKey Endpoint, CASCADE, related_name=status_endpoint) - target endpoint
Endpoint_Status.finding (ForeignKey Finding, CASCADE, related_name=status_finding) - associated finding
test_vectors: Input: 'http://example.com' -> protocol=http, userinfo=None, host=example.com, port=80 (inferred), path=None, query=None, fragment=None
Input: 'https://api.example.com:8443/v1/users?filter=active#section1' -> protocol=https, host=api.example.com, port=8443, path=v1/users, query=filter=active, fragment=section1, userinfo=None
Input: '//user:pass@localhost:3000/admin' -> userinfo=user:pass, host=localhost, port=3000, path=admin, protocol=None
Input: 'ftp://ftp.example.org/pub/file.txt?type=a' -> protocol=ftp, host=ftp.example.org, port=21 (inferred), path=pub/file.txt, query=type=a
Input: 'https://192.168.1.1' -> protocol=https, host=192.168.1.1, port=443 (inferred), path=None, query=None
Input: 'https://[::1]:8080/path' -> protocol=https, host=::1 (IPv6), port=8080, path=path
Input: '//example.com:80' with protocol=http -> port stored as null (matches default), query=null&port=null filter matches
Input: 'https://example.com:443/path?a=1&b&c=3' -> query parsed as 'a=1&b&c=3' (preserves valueless params)
Equality: Endpoint(host=x, product=p1) == Endpoint(host=x, product=p1) if str() matches and product_id matches
Equality: Endpoint(host=x, product=None) == Endpoint(host=x, product=None) if str() matches (product_id both None)
Hash: hash(ep) == hash(str(ep)) for use in sets/dicts
Endpoint_Status: mitigated=True + mitigated_by=user + mitigated_time=2024-01-15T10:30:00Z marks vulnerability resolved
Endpoint_Status: false_positive=True + mitigated=False indicates non-exploitable finding
Endpoint_Status: risk_accepted=True allows known-risk findings to be tracked with audit trail
edge_cases: Null protocol: from_uri('//host/path') returns protocol=None, __str__() strips dummy scheme prefix
Default port inference: from_uri('http://example.com:80') returns port=80 explicitly; endpoint_filter() matches both null and 80 when protocol=http
Port out of range: clean() raises ValidationError if port < 0 or >= 65536
Leading slash in path: clean() strips all leading slashes (root-less path), raises ValueError if path[0]==/
Query parameter format: from_uri() splits on & and handles both key=value and valueless keys; query_string reconstructs with &
Fragment handling: from_uri() caps at 500 chars, clean() removes leading #
Userinfo with colon: stored as 'user:password' in single field (not split), clean() validates per RFC3986
URL reconstruction: __str__() may fail hyperlink.normalize() and falls back to manual concatenation
Duplicate endpoints: endpoint_get_or_create() logs warning if >1 match exists (data corruption case)
Broken endpoints: endpoint.is_broken property returns True if clean() raises or product is None
IPv6 normalization: host=[::1] validated via validate_ipv46_address() in clean()
NULL character injection: clean() replaces 0x00 and \x00 with %00 for Postgres compatibility
Empty path/query/fragment: clean() converts empty strings to None (null)
Product scope: endpoint_filter() matches by product_id, endpoint equality includes product_id check if both non-null
Endpoint_Status unique constraint: (finding, endpoint) pair is unique per model Meta.constraints
result.label: endpoint

fields: severity_counts: {critical: u32, high: u32, medium: u32, low: u32, info: u32, total: u32}
status_counts: {open: u32, closed: u32, accepted: u32}
temporal_buckets: {period: Week|Month, grouped_date: Date, critical: u32, high: u32, medium: u32, low: u32, info: u32, total: u32, closed: u32}
age_buckets: {age_under_30: u32, age_31_60: u32, age_61_90: u32, age_90_plus: u32}
product_summary: {product_name: String, product_id: u32, critical: u32, high: u32, medium: u32, low: u32, info: u32, total: u32}
trending_opened: [u32; 12] (monthly for past 12 months from period start)

engineer_metrics: {month: {open: severity_counts, closed: severity_counts, accepted: severity_counts}, week: {open: severity_counts, closed: severity_counts, accepted: severity_counts}, age_buckets_high_critical: age_buckets}
key_behaviors: severity_count() applies identical counting logic across Finding and Endpoint_Status querysets using severity_lookup enum (severity vs finding__severity)
Counts match filter set: (Critical|High|Medium|Low|Info) in field, plus total of all 5 severity levels
Status buckets: Open=OPEN_FINDINGS_QUERY filter, Closed=CLOSED_FINDINGS_QUERY+mitigated range, Accepted=ACCEPTED_FINDINGS_QUERY+date range
Date range extracted from queryset min/max date field; timezone-aware datetime converted from date triplet (year,month,day)
Temporal aggregation: TruncWeek/TruncMonth groups by period, severity_count() called on grouped values, then filled with zero-data for missing periods
Period count: weeks_between=max((end_date-start_date).days//7, 2), months_between=max((end_date-start_date).months, 2)
Age calculation: ExtractDay(Coalesce(mitigated, NOW()) - date), then buckets: [0-30], [31-60], [61-90], [91+] days
Findings-per-product: Group by test__engagement__product (id+name), apply severity_count annotate
Top 10 products: Sort by critical desc, then high desc, medium desc, low desc; filter active=true, risk_accepted=false, verified status conditional
Closed findings use mitigated__date range (not discovery date); accepted findings filtered by risk_acceptance records
Monthly/weekly opened_per_period includes closed count when include_closed=true; derived from is_mitigated|mitigated boolean per metrics_type
Trending: 12 consecutive month buckets iterated backward from period start, each gets opened_in_period count
test_vectors: TEST: severity_count basic (5 findings, 1 each severity) -> critical:1, high:1, medium:1, low:1, info:1, total:5

TEST: status buckets (100 findings total, date 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31): date range Jan 1 00:00 to Mar 31 23:59; open_findings count all with mitigated__isnull=True, active=True, risk_accepted=False in date range; closed_findings count all with is_mitigated=True, mitigated__isnull=False, mitigated in [2024-01-01, now()]; accepted_findings count risk_accepted=True in date range -> expected: open:70, closed:20, accepted:10

TEST: age buckets (30 open findings all Critical|High, dates varying): dated 2024-01-15 (days_old=135 vs 2024-05-30): expect age_under_30:2 (May 1-30), age_31_60:6 (Apr 1-30), age_61_90:10 (Mar 1-31), age_90_plus:12 (before Mar 1)

TEST: weekly aggregate Jan-Mar 2024 (13 weeks span): start_date=2024-01-01, period_count=13, TruncWeek groups by Mon 00:00, each week row: grouped_date, critical, high, medium, low, info, total, closed (if include_closed); missing weeks filled with zeros
TEST: monthly aggregate Jan-Dec 2024 (12 months): start_date=2024-01-01, end_date=2024-12-31, period_count=12, TruncMonth groups by 1st of month, 12 rows for Jan-Dec, missing months filled with zeros

TEST: product summary top-10 (findings: {prod1: 5 critical+3 high, prod2: 2 critical+8 high, prod3: 0 critical+15 high}, active/unaccepted): sort by (-critical, -high, -medium, -low) -> [prod1 (crit:5, high:3), prod2 (crit:2, high:8), prod3 (crit:0, high:15)]

TEST: findings-per-product with severity breakdown: 3 products, 10 findings total distributed -> annotate product_name, product_id, then severity_count each group -> {product_name, product_id, critical, high, medium, low, info, total}

TEST: opened_in_period_list 12-month trend: given period Feb 2024-Jan 2025, iterate backward 12 months (Feb 2024, Jan 2024, Dec 2023, ..., Feb 2023), each calls opened_in_period(start, end) returning count of date in [start,end) -> list of 12 counts in chronological order

TEST: engineer metrics for user Jan 2024: month_start=2024-01-01, month_end=2024-02-01, open_month=reporter_findings with date in [Jan 1, Feb 1), closed_month=mitigated_by findings with mitigated in [Jan 1, Feb 1), accepted_month=risk_acceptance__owner=user, created in [Jan 1, Feb 1), each filtered by verified status -> {open: severity_dict, closed: severity_dict, accepted: severity_dict}
edge_cases: Date range extraction fails (no findings) -> default to (timezone.now(), timezone.now())
Empty queryset for period -> TruncWeek/TruncMonth aggregate still returns 0 for all severities + filled zeros
Mitigated date after latest discovery date -> still counted in closed_in_period (uses timezone.now() as upper bound)
Finding with unknown severity (not in Critical|High|Medium|Low|Info) -> included in total but not in severity-specific buckets
Age calculation with NULL mitigated -> uses NOW() as mitigated date (finding still open)
Timezone conversion: date triplet -> datetime with tzinfo=timezone.get_current_timezone()
Verified status filtering: conditional on settings enforce_verified_status OR enforce_verified_status_metrics; if either true, findings MUST have verified=True
Top 10 products: if fewer than 10 unique products, return all; ordering (critical desc, high desc, medium desc, low desc) is stable
Weekly period start: first day of week = Monday 00:00 (weekday offset -start_date.weekday())
Monthly period start: 1st of month 00:00
Period count minimum: max(calculated_periods, 2) ensures at least 2 periods in range
Risk accepted findings: appear in accepted bucket if risk_acceptance record exists and created in date range
Active=true filter in open findings: explicit active=True check, separate from risk_accepted=False
Duplicate/false_positive/out_of_scope: all filtered OUT in metrics queries (checked early in querysets)
result.label: metrics

key_behaviors: CSV parser deduplicates findings by SHA256(severity|title|description) hash, merging duplicates and incrementing nb_occurences
Boolean fields parsed from CSV via: val.lower()[0:1] == 't', defaulting to False if missing
Date fields parsed with dateutil.parser.parse() to flexible ISO formats, then .date() for date-only fields
Severity normalized to one of {Info, Low, Medium, High, Critical}; unknown values default to Info
Endpoint URLs can omit scheme; parser prepends '//' if missing '://', then creates Endpoint.from_uri()
CVE/CWE can come from cve/cwe fields (JSON) or CVE/CweId columns (CSV); collected into unsaved_vulnerability_ids
CVSS vectors parsed with external cvss_parser.parse_cvss_from_text(); stores clean_vector() result
JSON has strict allow-list of 55+ fields (includes required: title, severity, description); raises ValueError on unknown fields
Mitigated datetime parsed with dateutil, IsMitigated boolean separate; optional columns default to False/None if missing
JSON supports base64-encoded file attachments with optional titles; CSV only supports Url endpoints
fields: severity: string enum {Info, Low, Medium, High, Critical} (required)
date: ISO 8601 or flexible date string, parsed to date object
active: boolean (CSV: first char 't'/'f', JSON: direct bool)
mitigated: ISO 8601 datetime string, parsed to datetime object
endpoints: array of strings or objects (JSON only)
files: array of {data: base64, title: string} (JSON only)
kev_date: ISO 8601 datetime (CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities date)
test_vectors: JSON critical SQL injection: {title:'SQL Injection',severity:'Critical',description:'SQL injection in login',date:'2026-05-30',cve:'CVE-2024-1234',cwe:89,active:true,verified:true,cvssv3:'CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H',cvssv3_score:9.8} → parsed with cve in unsaved_vulnerability_ids, date as date object

CSV XSS finding: Title='XSS',Description='Script injection',Date='2026-05-28',Severity='High',Active='TRUE',CweId='79',CVE='CVE-2024-5678' → active=True, cwe=79, severity='High', unsaved_vulnerability_ids=['CVE-2024-5678']
CSV boolean parsing: Active='false' (lowercase) → True; Active='FALSE' → True; Active='no' → False; Active missing → False
CSV severity normalization: Severity='Critical' → 'Critical'; Severity='CRITICAL' → 'Info'; Severity='High' → 'High'; Severity='Unknown' → 'Info'
CSV endpoint parsing: Url='https://example.com' → Endpoint.from_uri('https://example.com'); Url='example.com' → Endpoint.from_uri('//example.com')
CSV deduplication: Two findings with same (severity,title,description) hash → merged with nb_occurences=2, endpoints/vulns extended
JSON endpoints: endpoints=['https://example.com','example.com'] → two LocationData.url objects with auto-scheme-prepend
JSON CVE field: {cve:'CVE-2024-1234'} → unsaved_vulnerability_ids=['CVE-2024-1234']
JSON vulnerability_ids: {vulnerability_ids:['CVE-2024-1234','CVE-2024-5678']} → unsaved_vulnerability_ids updated with both IDs
edge_cases: CSV missing required columns: Title/Description/Date/Severity → DictReader KeyError on missing header
CSV Duplicate column missing → defaults to False
JSON missing required field (title/severity/description) → ValueError with list of missing fields
JSON unknown field present → ValueError with list of disallowed field names
Severity not in enum → defaults to 'Info' (both CSV and JSON)
Date parsing failure → dateutil.parser raises ParserError if unparseable
Boolean value starts with 'T' (uppercase) → True; 'true'/'TRUE' → True; 'yes'/'Y' → True; anything else → False
CWE non-integer (CSV) → int() conversion error raised
CVSS vector with no valid CVSS match → cvss_parser returns empty list, field not populated
Endpoint URL with invalid characters → Endpoint.from_uri() raises validation exception
CVE field empty string → still added to unsaved_vulnerability_ids as empty string
Mitigated field without IsMitigated → mitigated datetime set independently
File data not valid base64 (JSON) → base64.b64decode() raises error
Tags field as string instead of array (JSON) → Finding(**item) assignment error
nb_occurences in CSV → only auto-incremented on dedup merge; if provided in JSON, used as-is
result.label: generic

result.module: DefectDojo Scanner Parsers: Grype and Gitleaks
key_behaviors: Grype: Aggregates findings by default using dupe_key of 'vuln_id|artifact_name|artifact_version'; detailed mode adds file_path to key for per-location deduplication
Grype severity is mapped via _convert_severity() - Unknown/Negligible become Info, others are title-cased
Grype extracts CVE/CWE via vuln_id field (e.g., CVE-2024-1234); related vulnerabilities are collected into vulnerability_ids list
Grype extracts package info from artifact object: name, version, purl; file_path from artifact.locations[0].path
Grype CVSS3 extracted from cvss array via cvss_parser.parse_cvss_from_text(vector), must be CVSS3 object
Gitleaks supports two JSON formats: legacy (has 'rule' field) and current (has 'Description' field)
Gitleaks severity is hardcoded High, escalated to Critical if 'Github', 'AWS', or 'Heroku' found in rule/description
Gitleaks title always prefixed with 'Hard coded' + reason/description, appended with filepath
Gitleaks always sets CWE to 798 (Use of Hard-Coded Credentials); no CVE extraction
Gitleaks deduplication uses hash(offender+file_path+line) for legacy, md5(title+secret+line) for current format
Gitleaks no_occurences tracks multiple occurrences; finding descriptions concatenated with '***' separator for duplicates
fields: Grype - Finding: title, description, severity, component_name, component_version, vuln_id_from_tool, cvssv3, epss_score, epss_percentile, mitigation, references, file_path, fix_available, fix_version, nb_occurences, unique_id_from_tool (detailed mode), unsaved_tags, unsaved_vulnerability_ids, unsaved_locations
Gitleaks Legacy - Finding: title, description, severity, cwe (798), file_path, line, dynamic_finding (false), static_finding (true), nb_occurences, unsaved_tags
Gitleaks Current - Finding: title, description, severity (High), cwe (798), file_path, line, dynamic_finding (false), static_finding (true), nb_occurences, unsaved_tags
test_vectors: Grype input: {"matches": [{"vulnerability": {"id": "CVE-2024-1234", "namespace": "nvd", "severity": "high", "description": "Test vuln", "urls": ["https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-1234"], "cvss": [{"vector": "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/AV:N/AU:N/C:H/I:H/A:H"}]}, "artifact": {"name": "log4j-core", "version": "2.14.1", "purl": "pkg:maven/org.apache.logging.log4j/log4j-core@2.14.1", "locations": [{"path": "app/lib/log4j.jar"}]}, "matchDetails": {"matcher": "pom-matcher"}, "relatedVulnerabilities": []}] } => Finding(title='CVE-2024-1234 in log4j-core:2.14.1', severity='High', component_name='log4j-core', component_version='2.14.1', vuln_id_from_tool='CVE-2024-1234', cvssv3='CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/AV:N/AU:N/C:H/I:H/A:H')

Gitleaks Legacy input: [{"rule": "AWS Manager ID", "file": "src/config.py", "commit": "abc123", "commitMessage": "Add credentials", "date": "2024-01-15", "author": "Alice", "email": "alice@example.com", "lineNumber": 42, "line": "aws_key = 'AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE'", "offender": "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE"}] => Finding(title='Hard Coded AWS Manager ID', severity='Critical', cwe=798, file_path='src/config.py', line=42)

Gitleaks Current input: [{"Description": "AWS API Key", "File": "src/app.js", "StartLine": "10", "Match": "aws_secret_access_key", "Secret": "wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG", "Commit": "def456", "Date": "2024-02-01", "Message": "Setup AWS client", "RuleID": "aws-key", "Tags": ["aws", "credentials"]}] => Finding(title='Hard coded AWS API Key found in src/app.js', severity='High', cwe=798, file_path='src/app.js', line=10)
edge_cases: Grype: severity 'Unknown' or 'Negligible' mapped to 'Info'; null characters stripped with .replace('\x00', '')
Grype: matchDetails can be dict or list; empty list results in no matcher tags
Grype: artifact_location empty list falls back to file_path=None
Grype: related_vulnerabilities pulls first match only for rel_cvss and rel_epss; epss fallback chain tries vuln then rel then back to vuln
Gitleaks Legacy: tags parsed from space/comma-separated string split(', '); missing lineNumber sets line=None
Gitleaks Current: StartLine converted to int, defaults to 0 if falsy; secret redaction via REDACTED string in legacy mode only
Gitleaks: dupe detection uses SHA256 (legacy) or MD5 (current); collision on same offender+file_path+line or title+secret+line dedupes findings
Gitleaks: formatting vulnerability - description string concatenation assumes trailing newline removal at end
result.label: extra-parsers
